title: Which response policy contains the dependency failure?
description: Select an injected incident and an application response. The visible outcomes come from a fixed game-day fixture, so the comparison teaches causality without pretending to forecast your workload.
evidenceNotice: These are synthetic, internally consistent fixture observations from the same 200 req/s workload and 100-worker pool. A real experiment must preserve the workload, build, topology, and measurement window when comparing policies.

scenarios.label: Payment calls stall for 1.8 seconds
scenarios.detail: Forty percent of payment requests reach a slow dependency path.

scenarios.label: Payment connections reset
scenarios.detail: Half of new dependency connections fail before a response is returned.
scenarios.injectedFault: Connection reset on 50% of new calls

scenarios.label: One payment zone disappears
scenarios.detail: Healthy traffic shifts to fewer instances while existing connections drain.
scenarios.injectedFault: One of three dependency zones unavailable

policies.label: Wait and retry twice
policies.detail: Use a long timeout and retry inside the same request path without isolation.
policies.path: Long wait → two retries → shared worker pool

policies.label: Bound the timeout
policies.detail: Fail the dependency call at 350ms and do not retry synchronously.

policies.label: Breaker plus bounded fallback
policies.detail: Open after the error threshold, isolate probes, and return a degraded but valid response.

outcomes.title: Retries preserve some successes but exhaust the worker budget
outcomes.explanation: Slow attempts remain in flight, retries add more work, and the shared worker pool queues unrelated checkouts. A high success rate hides an unsafe latency and saturation boundary.
outcomes.userResult: Checkout stalls spread beyond the faulty dependency calls

outcomes.title: The timeout protects capacity but exposes dependency failure
outcomes.explanation: Workers return quickly enough to avoid saturation, but affected users receive an error because no alternate response exists. Capacity protection and product continuity are separate decisions.
outcomes.userResult: Affected checkouts fail quickly instead of hanging

outcomes.title: The breaker prevents repeated waits and the fallback preserves the user path
outcomes.explanation: A small probe set tests recovery while most affected calls take a bounded degraded path. The result stays inside the fixture's success, latency, and utilization objectives.
outcomes.userResult: Checkout continues with a clearly degraded payment option

outcomes.title: Immediate retries amplify the reset storm
outcomes.explanation: Every failed connection creates another attempt while the dependency is already unstable. Recovery traffic competes with fresh work and pushes the shared pool beyond its guardrail.
outcomes.userResult: Retries turn a partial reset fault into broad checkout delay

outcomes.title: Fast failure keeps the service responsive but loses the affected operation
outcomes.explanation: The service remains available to healthy requests because it does not retry. Without a fallback or asynchronous recovery path, the dependency error is still user-visible.
outcomes.userResult: Healthy calls remain fast while reset calls fail

outcomes.title: Isolation stops the reset loop and preserves bounded service
outcomes.explanation: The breaker stops most connection attempts, controlled probes detect recovery, and the fallback handles the product path without adding a retry wave.
outcomes.userResult: Most users receive the bounded fallback while recovery is probed

outcomes.title: Retries consume the reserve capacity needed for failover
outcomes.explanation: Traffic shifts to surviving zones while retries duplicate work. The policy makes the capacity loss harder to recover from and expands the incident beyond the failed zone.
outcomes.userResult: Surviving zones saturate and all checkout traffic slows

outcomes.title: The timeout limits queue growth but cannot replace missing capacity
outcomes.explanation: The service stays below the utilization guardrail, yet the remaining zones cannot meet the success objective. Capacity reserve and placement must be tested separately from timeout behavior.
outcomes.userResult: The service stays responsive but rejects excess demand

outcomes.title: The fallback protects users, but the capacity objective still fails
outcomes.explanation: Isolation contains repeated calls and keeps latency bounded. The fixture remains below its success objective, showing that an application policy cannot substitute for independent capacity and placement.
outcomes.userResult: Most users continue, but some requests exceed available capacity
